english.title: Make linked gaming machines available for use - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) made a gaming machine available for use by another, and the amount or value of the prize available through use of the gaming machine was or may have been wholly or partly determined by reference to use made of another linked gaming machine
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 244 and 246(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
made a gaming machine available for use by another
the amount/value of a prize available through use of the first gaming machine
was/may have been wholly/partly
determined by reference to the use of another linked gaming machine

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 244(2) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that the offence does not apply where the person who makes the first gaming machine available for use is the holder of a casino premises licence and the first gaming machine and the linked gaming machine are situated on the same premises.
(ii) For the territorial application of this section see section 251 of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
